.. _arduino_tft_clock:

======================
1.5 TFT Digital Clock
======================

Displaying a digital clock on the TFT LCD screen using the TFT_eSPI library.

Overview
========

This project brings the TFT display to life by drawing a digital clock face. You'll learn how to use the **TFT_eSPI** library to draw shapes, text, and create a custom user interface on a 320x240 SPI display.

What You'll Learn
=================

* Initializing the TFT display via SPI
* Drawing rectangles, lines, and text on screen
* Using custom fonts with TFT_eSPI
* Simple time-keeping with ``millis()``

Pin Connections
===============

The TFT display uses the following SPI pins (pre-configured in ``User_Setup.h`` of TFT_eSPI):

======== ========
TFT      ESP32-S3
======== ========
MOSI     GPIO 11
SCLK     GPIO 12
CS       GPIO 10
DC       GPIO 13
RST      GPIO 9
BL       GPIO 3
======== ========

How the Code Works
==================

The sketch uses TFT_eSPI to render a watch-style interface:

.. code-block:: cpp

   TFT_eSPI tft = TFT_eSPI();
   tft.begin();
   tft.setRotation(1);  // Landscape

   // Draw background
   tft.fillScreen(TFT_WHITE);
   tft.fillRoundRect(10, 10, 300, 220, 15, TFT_DARKGREY);

   // Display time with 7-segment font
   tft.setTextColor(TFT_GREEN, TFT_DARKGREY);
   tft.drawString("12:30", 60, 60, 7);

The clock starts from the compile time and advances each second using ``millis()``. The display shows hours and minutes on the top row, and seconds below.

Expected Result
===============

After uploading, the TFT screen displays a digital clock with a watch-style bezel design. The time advances every second.
